pointers.sentence: 6.1 replaced the blank choice's dashes with a label "more accessible and translatable" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
5.0 made the division layout the default, which the 4.1 notes had recommended as "easier for screen reader users to navigate" (`docs/releases/4.1.txt`).
Since 5.0 a form rendered as a string uses `BaseRenderer.form_template_name`, `"django/forms/div.html"` (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.template_name`).
It also removed BaseForm's _html_output, which drew the layouts in Python before 4.0 (`docs/releases/4.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.0.txt`).
It also removed BaseForm's _html_output, which drew the layouts in Python before 4.0 (`docs/releases/4.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.0.txt`).

The division template prints each visible field's `RenderableFieldMixin.as_field_group` (5.0), which draws label, help text, errors and widget from the field's template, by default `"django/forms/field.html"` (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.template_name`; [Rendering a form: renderers and templates](../forms/rendering.md#the-built-in-templates)).
A project whose setting still names one gets it, with a warning, under 5.2.17; since 6.0 the import fails (`django/forms/renderers.py:get_default_renderer`):
5.1 put it on the `<fieldset>` drawn around a widget whose `Widget.use_fieldset` is true (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.1.txt`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).
5.1 put it on the `<fieldset>` drawn around a widget whose `Widget.use_fieldset` is true (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.1.txt`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).
5.1 put it on the `<fieldset>` drawn around a widget whose `Widget.use_fieldset` is true (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.1.txt`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).
At this commit `BoundField.aria_describedby` (5.2) gives the ids of the help text and errors the field has (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.aria_describedby`).
`BoundField.build_widget_attrs` puts them on the input unless the attribute is given or the widget asks for a fieldset (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.build_widget_attrs`).

The error list takes its id from `ErrorList.field_id` (5.2), which `BaseForm.add_error` sets (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.add_error`; [`BoundField`: a field in a form](../forms/bound-fields.md#the-attributes-a-bound-field-adds)).
Since 6.0 a form's URL field by default puts `"https"` in front of a value with no scheme, where it put `"http"` (`django/forms/fields.py:URLField.to_python`).
5.0 made the scheme the argument `assume_scheme=` and deprecated its default (`django/forms/fields.py:URLField.__init__`).
`get_blank_choice_label` gives it: `BLANK_CHOICE_LABEL`, translated, or the dashes of `BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` while `USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` is true (`django/db/models/utils.py:get_blank_choice_label`).
Since 6.1, setting `USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` warns (`django/conf/__init__.py`).

Reading `BLANK_CHOICE_DASH`, a plain constant, warned under no release (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:BLANK_CHOICE_DASH`; [Choices: `ChoiceField`, `ModelChoiceField` and the choice widgets](../forms/choices.md#the-blank-choices-label)).
Since 6.1, `ModelChoiceField.__init__` defaults `empty_label=` to `""` and replaces `""` with the blank choice's label (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField.__init__`).
Only the constructor does this: an `empty_label` set to `""` after the field is made is drawn as it is (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceIterator.__iter__`).
In 6.2 `EmailValidator` checks an address in methods a subclass can replace (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).
`EmailValidator.validate` hands the user part to `EmailValidator.validate_username` and the domain to `EmailValidator.validate_domain` (`django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.validate`).

These two raise `ValidationError` with their part as the parameter `"username"` or `"domain"` (`django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.validate_username`, `django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.validate_domain`).

These two raise `ValidationError` with their part as the parameter `"username"` or `"domain"` (`django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.validate_username`, `django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.validate_domain`).
A subclass that defines it warns as the class is made (`django/core/validators.py:EmailValidator.__init_subclass__`).
`validate` then calls it in place of `validate_domain` ([Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md#domain-names-urls-and-email-addresses)).

| `bound_field_class` | New in 5.2: on a form field, a form or a renderer, the class of bound field; before, only an override of `Field.get_bound_field` chose one | `django/forms/fields.py:Field.get_bound_field` |
| `ErrorList`, `ErrorDict` | Since 5.0, a plain string from their rendering is escaped; 4.0 had deprecated it | `django/template/base.py:render_value_in_context` |
| `Script` | New in 5.2: a `Media` asset for a script, with HTML attributes; since 6.1, a script's path given as a string becomes one | `django/forms/widgets.py:Media._normalize_js` |
| `Stylesheet` | New in 6.1: a `Media` asset for a stylesheet, with HTML attributes; a stylesheet's path given as a string becomes one | `django/forms/widgets.py:Media._normalize_css` |
| `FilePathField.set_choices` | New in 6.1: scans the directory; the field's `__init__` calls it, and a form's `__init__` may call it again | `django/forms/fields.py:FilePathField.set_choices` |
| `BaseModelFormSet.save_existing` | Since 5.0, its second argument is `obj=`, once `instance=`; Django passes it by position | `django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.save_existing_objects` |
| `StepValueValidator` | New in 5.0: `offset=`, a value to count the steps from; the form `IntegerField` and its subclasses give their `min_value` | `django/forms/fields.py:IntegerField.__init__` |

| `DomainNameValidator` | New in 5.1: validates a domain name, as does `validate_domain_name`; `URLValidator` and `EmailValidator` take its host-name patterns | `django/core/validators.py:DomainNameValidator` |
